question: Why do plant cells have cell walls?

options.text: They protect the plant cells from various environmental factors
They do not have cell membrane

solution:
The correct answer is **__option1__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

 
• **Structural Support**: The cell wall provides rigidity and strength, maintaining the overall shape of the cell.
 
• **Protection**: It acts as a protective barrier against mechanical damage, pathogens, and environmental stressors.
 
• **Water Regulation**: The cell wall helps regulate water balance, preventing excessive water uptake.
 
• **Transport and Communication**: Plasmodesmata in the cell wall allow **communication and nutrient** transport between adjacent cells.
 
• **Cell-to-Cell Adhesion**: It ensures adhesion between neighboring cells, holding them together as tissues.
 
• **Storage**: Some plant cells store substances within their cell walls, which can be accessed when needed.
